title: Consortium Accord — LegalTech outreach scratchpad
content:
Topline: Consortium Accord (mid-stage legaltech startup building contract automation + precedent library). Potential partner/early customer for Redwood inference: contract clause extraction, summarization, precedent search, and auto-drafting using private models. 

Why them: product-led sales motion, heavy document processing, strong regulatory/compliance needs (enterprise customers), likely to benefit from Private deployment or Dedicated due to PII/legal docs. Their pitch to customers emphasizes accuracy + audit trail — matches our strengths (private deployment + audit logs + rollout controls).

Primary contacts (scoped from LinkedIn + demo notes):
- Priya Narang — Head of Product (ex-LexisNexis, focuses on corp legal workflows)
- Aaron Feld — CTO (former infra lead at a marketplace, cares about latency and cost)
- Pri LegalOps — not clear yet, need to surface (likely buyer for compliance features)

Decision signals to watch for:
- Public mention of scaling NLP for contracts (>10k docs/day)
- Enterprise pilot with a BigLaw or F500 legal ops team
- Requests for data residency or on-prem hints at Private interest

Initial hypothesis of Redwood fit:
- POC type: contract clause extraction + redact + precedent search (embedding + retrieval + safe summarization).
- Minimum viable architecture: Upload pipeline (S3 -> Redwood embeddings) + retrieval layer (approx nearest neighbors), generation endpoint for summaries via Hosted or Dedicated (private if required for security).
- Value props to emphasize: deterministic latency SLA for review workflows, audit trails for model outputs, controlled rollouts so legal can validate output quality per corpus.

Cold email variants (short -> medium -> long). Pick tone: consultative, mention redwood-specific ROI signals.
Subject lines: "Quality + audit for contract ML at Consortium Accord" / "Pilot: low-risk contract summarization (Redwood)"
Cold email (short):
Hi Priya —
Saw Consortium Accord’s new precedent search feature — nice. We help legal teams run contract extraction + summarization with predictable latency and audit logs (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private options). Quick question: are you evaluating vendor models or planning an on-prem/private POC for high-sensitivity clients?
— Maya (Redwood)

Longer variant (if ~linked-in reply):
Hi Priya —
Congrats on the precedent search launch. A lot of legal teams tell us they want model outputs they can trace and test against gold prompts. We offer:
- deterministically fast inference with cost controls (batching & caching tuned per workload)
- per-request audit logs and model version pinning
- private deployments and key management for regulated clients
Would love 20–30 minutes to share a short pilot plan (30k docs, 4–6 week POC, success metric = 90% precision on clause extraction + 20% reviewer time saved). Any interest?

Call script / discovery bullets:
- Confirm volumes: docs/day, avg tokens/doc, peak review concurrency.
- Who is the buyer? LegalOps vs Security vs CTO? Procurement timeline?
- Where do they want data to live? (Hosted allowed? VPC? On-prem?)
- Current model stack: open models, vendor LLMs, custom fine-tune?
- Acceptance criteria for pilot (accuracy thresholds, auditability, SLA).
- Red flags: client wants complete model ownership AND zero vendor network access (air-gapped). If so, escalate Private on-prem talk.

Objections and suggested rebuttals (raw):
- "We already use X model provider / vendor": acknowledge. "Great — we often complement by running a deterministic inference tier for high-sensitivity clients (pin a vetted model) and fallback to lower-cost variants for bulk processing. Can we run a controlled comparison on a slice of your corpora?"
- "Concerned about PII / compliance": empathize + list: "Private deployment, KMS/HSM integrations, per-request audit logs, and optional schema-level redaction pipeline. We can show architecture + SOC2 controls and run a redaction test during POC."
- "Cost": propose staged approach: "Start with a dedicated small cluster for pilot (committed for 4–6 weeks), measure reviewer time saved and then model per-token cost reductions via batching/quantization recommendations from Redwood Optimize."
- "Quality inconsistency": present rollout approach: "Canary generation, prompt/regression tests, and auto-fallback to baseline model when quality drops. We tie regressions to prompt suites so Legal can approve before further rollout."

Technical checklist (what I need to prep before POC):
- Sample dataset: 500–1,000 redacted contracts + labeling for clause types (CSV/JSONL).
- Desired outputs: clause extraction schema, summary length limits, redaction rules.
- SSO + SCIM for pilot users (prod parity).
- LegalOps acceptance criteria doc (simple spreadsheet).
- Estimate avg_tokens/doc and expected concurrency so we can size Dedicated pool.

POC outline (4–6 weeks):
Week 0: Kickoff + security review + access (S3 bucket, IAM roles)
Week 1: Data ingestion + baseline runs on hosted API; simple metric capture (precision/recall)
Week 2: Model tuning (prompt templates, retrieval config), build retrieval embeddings & vector store
Week 3: Dedicated cluster sizing + latency testing; run audit/logging validations
Week 4: Acceptance testing with legal reviewers; collect reviewer time/QA metrics
Optional Week 5–6: Private deployment if required + handover docs
Success metric: >= 90% precision on clause classification OR >= 20% reduction in reviewer time for redaction/summarization tasks.

Competition: likely players are legal-specific vendors (EigenDocs?), general LLM vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic), and enterprise search vendors. Differentiator = ability to combine private deployments + operational rollouts + cost/perf controls (Optimize recommendations).

Ask from me (Maya):
- Get network intro to Priya (Ethan or Sofia may know someone).
- Pull a quick cost/latency sizing for 2 nodes (A100 equiv) for 500k tokens/day and expected pricing escalation. (JIRA-LGL-487 placeholder).
- Prepare a short slide (2–3) showing audit logs + model pinning + fallback flows for security review.

Outbound cadence (proposal):
Day 0: Short email variant
Day 3: LinkedIn note mentioning a signal (precedent launch)
Day 7: Follow up email with 1-pager + POC outline
Day 14: Offer 15-min intro + ask for preferred signal (volume or pilot owners)

Open questions / unknowns (need to surface in first call):
- Exact sample sizes they are comfortable sharing (redaction required?)
- If they have internal label sets already (saves time)
- Procurement windows / legal reviews timing

Quick reminders for outreach personalization:
- Call out precedent search launch by name + 1 sentence on how we could reduce manual precedent curation.
- For CTO outreach emphasize latency & cost controls. For Product emphasize audit + qualitative review flows. For LegalOps emphasize redact + traceability.

Next steps:
- Draft intro email & 1-pager (Ethan to review) — target EOD Wed
- Get sizing numbers from infra (Sofia) — target Thu
- Slack: #gttm-growth ping for intros (put context: "Consortium Accord — legaltech; Priya Narang")

Notes to self: keep this ultra-light, prospects like simple pilots. Don’t oversell: focus on measurable reviewer time saved and auditability.
